sources.title: Momentum Crashes
sources.claim: Momentum crashes are partly forecastable and are concentrated in panic states following market declines, when volatility is high and markets rebound.

sources.title: Momentum Has Its Moments
sources.claim: Momentum risk varies over time; volatility-based risk management materially reduces crash exposure in the studied equity momentum strategy.

sources.title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
sources.authors: Brian Hurst; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
sources.claim: Time-series momentum was positive on average across a very long multi-asset history and across varied macro environments.

sources.title: ... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
sources.authors: Campbell R. Harvey; Yan Liu; Heqing Zhu
sources.claim: Multiple testing materially raises the hurdle required to accept newly discovered return factors.

sources.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
sources.authors: David H. Bailey; Marcos Lopez de Prado
sources.claim: Reported Sharpe ratios should be adjusted for multiple trials, selection bias, and non-normal returns before treating a backtest as reliable.

sources.title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
sources.claim: Crypto markets exhibit recurrent cross-exchange price deviations; common signed-volume components explain a large share of Bitcoin returns in the study.

sources.title: Carry
sources.authors: Ralph S.J. Koijen; Tobias J. Moskowitz; Lasse Heje Pedersen; Evert B. Vrugt
sources.claim: Carry predicts returns across multiple asset classes but is exposed to recession, liquidity, and volatility risks.

rules.hypothesis: After a sharp decline in a high-volatility state, adding fresh short momentum exposure may have poor asymmetry because rebound risk rises.
rules.mechanism: Momentum crash / convex rebound risk after panic states.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS adaptation to crypto; thresholds are not taken from the paper and require out-of-sample validation.

rules.hypothesis: Momentum-derived exposure should be reduced when realized volatility is unusually high.
rules.mechanism: Time-varying momentum risk and crash exposure.
rules.formalization_note: Crypto threshold is a VERITAS hypothesis; validate by asset, horizon, and volatility regime.

rules.hypothesis: Positive medium-horizon own-price trend may carry continuation information.
rules.formalization_note: Directional crypto adaptation of multi-asset trend-following evidence.

rules.hypothesis: Negative medium-horizon own-price trend may carry continuation information.
rules.formalization_note: Directional crypto adaptation of multi-asset trend-following evidence.

rules.hypothesis: Material cross-venue price divergence should reduce confidence in a directional signal until fragmentation normalizes.
rules.formalization_note: This is a VERITAS execution/data-quality adaptation, not a verbatim trading rule from the paper.

rules.hypothesis: Strong aggressive-buy flow during elevated activity may contain short-horizon continuation information.
rules.formalization_note: Single-exchange taker flow is only a proxy for the paper's common signed-volume component; low prior until validated.

rules.hypothesis: New factors must clear a stricter evidence hurdle when many variants have been tested.
rules.formalization_note: Governance rule; never enters live directional committee directly.

rules.hypothesis: Backtest Sharpe must be deflated for selection bias, multiple trials, and non-normality before promotion.
rules.formalization_note: Governance rule; to be applied by the model-promotion pipeline.

rules.hypothesis: Crypto basis/funding may be studied as a carry-like characteristic, but directional mapping must be validated separately.
rules.formalization_note: Research agenda only; no live directional inference is made from general cross-asset carry evidence.
